name: Just Knew
tagline: You've been doing it for years. You just never called it that.
epigraph: A famous bartender's recipe for the classic behind this drink: build it in any order.
glassware: a rocks glass, filled with ice
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. The line that lands: "You'd never call those a practice, and they've been holding you up the whole time." Barnum watch: "it slips" is held by the shelf, the silent weekend, the inbox and the song in the car. History trimmed from 53% to 48% of yours. Fenced: *Anyway*'s tagline (Regan's "great night" gets one clause, no Thursday); *In a Minute* (stopping, time), *Nothing to It* (nerves), *Brought Home*, *Straight Back*, *For Good*, *Before the Room* ("calm", "at the door"). "Any order" appears twice (epigraph, y4), not in the name. Pronoun warnings accepted by Wren: every "he" and "his" in yours 1–4 is Gary Regan, never the guest. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/gary-regan-mindful-bartending.md` (Gary Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* (2018) pdf 114–121, 133, 351, his own account; the 2003 first edition's "in any order" via archive.org full-text search, secondary; *Oxford Companion* REGAN pdf 1633–1635; Robert Simonson, *A Proper Drink* pp. 62–63). Drink: *Liquid Intelligence* pdf 107–108, 135 (Negroni dilution and figures); *Cocktail Codex* printed 89–90, 94, 297; *Flavor Matrix* Citrus pdf 80–81 and Grape pdf 141 (laurel/bay on both wheels). Room notes: `work/explorer-magician/`.
names_note: **Just Knew**, the room's pick (all three, r5): from the one quote the reading keeps ("I just knew it worked"), and about the guest's habit that worked before it had a name. **Any Order** was Wren's pick until r5; she moved because with the epigraph and y4 it would say "any order" three times (Tomás). Also considered: *Second Nature* (Hester's second).
open_items: **The true order (Hester C1, C2):** the 1973 hour before shifts at Drake's Drum came first, with no name ("I just knew it worked"); decades later he looked back and called it "in effect, meditating", and the mindfulness-for-bartenders idea came to him at workshops. Nothing says he kept the hour every night for years (Simonson has him moving bar to bar).

**Advice vs practice (C3, C4):** "I'm breathing in. I'm breathing out" and the five-to-ten minutes are his advice to readers, not his 1973 habit; the Thursday regular is his example, not a memory. The breath-stir was dropped for that reason, and because a Negroni tolerates a wide range of dilution (*LI* pdf 107–108).

**"Any order" is in *Joy*, not verified in *The Negroni* (C10):** the 2015 book is not in the library or on archive.org; the reading says "in his best-known book". Counterweight (C11): PUNCH prints his Jägermeister riff stirred and strained, and Simonson has him stirring with his finger, so it's "the way he printed it", never "how he always made it". A gap for Robin: *The Negroni* (2015).

**Fenced against siblings (C7, C8):** *Anyway*'s tagline is his "great night" in other words, so it gets one clause; the Innocent family's Wise Kid row keeps *Joy* pdf 133 (the Scotch Sours, the waitress), all of which this pour leaves out. No death year, no faith, no wellness claim; Oxford never mentions mindfulness (C9), so the inward story rests on his own account.

**The drink is ours:** gin leading and half the vermouth dry (45 / 22.5 / 15 / 15) is our balance, not Arnold's allowance, which keeps vermouth one-to-one with Campari. Sugar sits at the sweet edge on purpose (5.95 g; Campari's bitterness, which balance.py can't hear); equal parts reads 9.49 g. The bay leaf is ours, not his. The cacao nib tincture was ruled out (a jar made specially, the *Codex*'s move, and it would have cost the veto-free floor: shared-plant nut and milk warnings).
